import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 9.78

by V. P. Shunkov

Does there exist a periodic residually finite $F^*$-group (see Archive, 7.42) all of whose
Sylow subgroups are finite and which is not binary finite?

Terminology. A group is *periodic* if every element has finite order. It is *residually
finite* if every non-identity element lies outside some normal subgroup of finite index.
It is *binary finite* if any two of its elements generate a finite subgroup. Following
Archive problem 7.42, a group $G$ is an *$F^*$-group* if for every finite subgroup $H$ of
$G$ and every element $a$ of prime order in $N_G(H)/H$, all the subgroups
$\langle a, a^g \rangle$ with $g \in N_G(H)/H$ are finite. A *Sylow $p$-subgroup* of an
arbitrary group is a maximal $p$-subgroup.

Problem 7.42 asked the same question without the residual finiteness hypothesis.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«9.78»

variable (G : Type*) [Group G]

/-- A group $G$ is *residually finite* if for every $g \neq 1$ in $G$ there is a normal
subgroup of finite index in $G$ not containing $g$. -/
def IsResiduallyFinite : Prop :=
  ∀ g : G, g ≠ 1 → ∃ N : Subgroup G, N.Normal ∧ N.FiniteIndex ∧ g ∉ N

/-- A group $G$ is *binary finite* if any two of its elements generate a finite subgroup. -/
def IsBinaryFinite : Prop :=
  ∀ a b : G, Finite (Subgroup.closure {a, b})

/-- A group $G$ is an *$F^*$-group* in the sense of V. P. Shunkov (Kourovka Notebook,
Archive, 7.42) if for every finite subgroup $H$ of $G$ and every element $a$ of prime order
in the quotient $N_G(H)/H$, the subgroups $\langle a, a^g \rangle$ are finite for all
$g \in N_G(H)/H$. Here $a^g = g^{-1} a g$. -/
def IsFStarGroup : Prop :=
  ∀ H : Subgroup G, Finite H →
    ∀ a g : H.normalizer ⧸ H.subgroupOf H.normalizer, (orderOf a).Prime →
      Finite (Subgroup.closure {a, g⁻¹ * a * g})

variable {G}

@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isResiduallyFinite_of_finite [Finite G] : IsResiduallyFinite G :=
  fun _ hg => ⟨⊥, inferInstance, inferInstance, by simpa using hg⟩

@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isBinaryFinite_of_finite [Finite G] : IsBinaryFinite G :=
  fun _ _ => inferInstance

@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isFStarGroup_of_finite [Finite G] : IsFStarGroup G :=
  fun _ _ _ _ _ => inferInstance

/--
Does there exist a periodic residually finite $F^*$-group (see Archive, 7.42) all of whose
Sylow subgroups are finite and which is not binary finite?

Sylow $p$-subgroups are the maximal $p$-subgroups; the condition is imposed on every Sylow
$p$-subgroup for every prime $p$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«9.78» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G),
      Monoid.IsTorsion G ∧ IsResiduallyFinite G ∧ IsFStarGroup G ∧
      (∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime → ∀ P : Sylow p G, Finite P) ∧ ¬ IsBinaryFinite G := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«9.78»
attempts.decomposition_objections: None. The single-slot decomposition with all conjuncts joined by ∧ under an existential is the correct reading of the yes/no question, and the file follows it.
modeling_decisions: The Archive 7.42 text is not in the sandbox and there is no network access, so the F*-group definition follows the decomposition notes together with Shunkov's standard terminology (F*-groups = 'conjugately biprimitively finite' groups): for every finite subgroup H (including the trivial one) and every element a of prime order in N_G(H)/H, ⟨a, a^g⟩ is finite for all g ∈ N_G(H)/H. A reviewer with access to the Archive should confirm this is verbatim the 7.42 definition.

N_G(H)/H is modelled as `H.normalizer ⧸ H.subgroupOf H.normalizer` (Mathlib's `Subgroup.normal_in_normalizer` provides the group structure); a^g is written g⁻¹ * a * g, and since g ranges over the whole quotient the choice of conjugation convention is immaterial.
'Element of prime order' is `(orderOf a).Prime`; infinite-order elements have orderOf 0, which is not prime, so they are correctly excluded.

'All Sylow subgroups are finite' is `∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime → ∀ P : Sylow p G, Finite P`, i.e. every maximal p-subgroup (Mathlib's `Sylow p G`, which exists for arbitrary groups) for every prime p; non-prime p is excluded because `IsPGroup` degenerates there.

Residual finiteness is stated in the standard 'separating normal subgroup of finite index' form (equivalent to the intersection of all finite-index normal subgroups being trivial, and to separation by homomorphisms to finite groups).
The group is quantified in `Type` (universe 0), matching the other Kourovka files (1_40, 1_74, 19_25, 20_76).

The three bespoke definitions are kept in the problem file (the task allows writing only one file); a maintainer may prefer moving IsResiduallyFinite and IsBinaryFinite to FormalConjecturesForMathlib. Three short `@[category test]` lemmas (finite groups satisfy each predicate) are included with proofs as basic API tests, per CONTRIBUTING.md.

subgroups are finite and which is not binary finite?

a Sylow $p$-subgroup means a maximal $p$-subgroup.

      IsResiduallyFinite G ∧
      IsFStarGroup G ∧

Shunkov's F*-condition is modeled as follows: for every finite subgroup H, every prime-order element a of N_G(H)/H, and every g in that quotient, the subgroup generated by a and g⁻¹ag is finite. import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 9.78

by V. P. Shunkov

Does there exist a periodic residually finite $F^*$-group all of whose Sylow
subgroups are finite and which is not binary finite?

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«9.78»

/-- A group is residually finite if every nonidentity element has nonidentity
image under a homomorphism to some finite group. -/
def IsResiduallyFinite (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ g : G, g ≠ 1 →
    ∃ (Q : Type) (_ : Group Q) (_ : Finite Q) (f : G →* Q), f g ≠ 1

/-- An $F^*$-group in the sense of Shunkov is a group $G$ such that, for every
finite subgroup $H$ of $G$, every subgroup of $N_G(H)/H$ generated by two
conjugate elements of prime order is finite. -/
def IsFStarGroup (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ H : Subgroup G, (H : Set G).Finite →
    let Q := H.normalizer ⧸ H.subgroupOf H.normalizer
    ∀ a : Q, (orderOf a).Prime → ∀ g : Q,
      ((Subgroup.closure {a, g⁻¹ * a * g} : Subgroup Q) : Set Q).Finite

/--
Does there exist a periodic residually finite $F^*$-group all of whose Sylow
subgroups are finite and which is not binary finite? Here periodic means that
every element has finite order, and binary finite means that every pair of
elements generates a finite subgroup.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«9.78» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G),
      (∀ g : G, IsOfFinOrder g) ∧
      IsResiduallyFinite G ∧
      IsFStarGroup G ∧
      (∀ (p : ℕ), p.Prime → ∀ P : Sylow p G, (P : Set G).Finite) ∧
      ¬ (∀ x y : G, ((Subgroup.closure {x, y} : Subgroup G) : Set G).Finite) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«9.78»
modeling_decisions: Residual finiteness is expressed by requiring every nonidentity element to have nonidentity image under a homomorphism to a finite group; surjectivity is unnecessary because the image is a finite quotient.

The Shunkov F*-condition is stated in the quotient H.normalizer ⧸ H.subgroupOf H.normalizer: for each prime-order element a and each quotient element g, the subgroup generated by a and g⁻¹ * a * g is finite.
Finiteness of subgroups is represented by Set.Finite for their carrier sets, avoiding proposition-valued typeclass quantification.
Periodicity is represented by ∀ g, IsOfFinOrder g. Mathlib's Sylow p G supplies maximal p-subgroups, with p explicitly restricted to primes.
Not binary finite is represented as the negation of the assertion that every pair generates a finite subgroup.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 9.78

by V. P. Shunkov

Does there exist a periodic residually finite $F^{*}$-group (see Archive, 7.42) all of
whose Sylow subgroups are finite and which is not binary finite?

Here a group $G$ is an $F^{*}$-group in the sense of V. P. Shunkov (Kourovka Notebook,
Archive, 7.42) if for every finite subgroup $H$ of $G$ and every element $a$ of prime order
in $N_G(H)/H$, all the subgroups $\langle a, a^g \rangle$, $g \in N_G(H)/H$, are finite.
A Sylow $p$-subgroup of an arbitrary group is a maximal $p$-subgroup. A group is
*binary finite* if any two of its elements generate a finite subgroup.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«9.78»

variable (G : Type*) [Group G]

/-- A group $G$ is *residually finite* if every non-identity element lies outside some
normal subgroup of finite index, i.e. the intersection of all normal subgroups of finite
index of $G$ is trivial. -/
def IsResiduallyFinite : Prop :=
  ∀ g : G, g ≠ 1 → ∃ N : Subgroup G, N.Normal ∧ N.FiniteIndex ∧ g ∉ N

/-- A group is *binary finite* if any two of its elements generate a finite subgroup. -/
def IsBinaryFinite : Prop :=
  ∀ x y : G, Finite (Subgroup.closure {x, y})

/-- A group $G$ is an *$F^{*}$-group* (V. P. Shunkov, Kourovka Notebook, Archive, 7.42) if
for every finite subgroup $H$ of $G$ and every element $a$ of prime order in the quotient
$N_G(H)/H$, the subgroups $\langle a, a^g \rangle$, $g \in N_G(H)/H$, are all finite. -/
def IsFStarGroup : Prop :=
  ∀ H : Subgroup G, Finite H →
    ∀ a g : H.normalizer ⧸ H.subgroupOf H.normalizer,
      (orderOf a).Prime → Finite (Subgroup.closure {a, g⁻¹ * a * g})

variable {G}

/-- A finite group is residually finite. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isResiduallyFinite_of_finite [Finite G] : IsResiduallyFinite G :=
  fun g hg => ⟨⊥, inferInstance, inferInstance, by simpa using hg⟩

/-- A finite group is binary finite. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isBinaryFinite_of_finite [Finite G] : IsBinaryFinite G :=
  fun _ _ => inferInstance

/-- A finite group is an $F^{*}$-group. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isFStarGroup_of_finite [Finite G] : IsFStarGroup G :=
  fun _ _ _ _ _ => inferInstance

/-- A binary finite group is an $F^{*}$-group. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem IsBinaryFinite.isFStarGroup (hG : IsBinaryFinite G) : IsFStarGroup G := by
  intro H _ a g _
  induction a using QuotientGroup.induction_on with | H a
  induction g using QuotientGroup.induction_on with | H g
  -- `⟨a, a^g⟩` is finite in `N_G(H)`: it embeds into the finite subgroup `⟨a, a^g⟩` of `G`.
  have h₁ : (Subgroup.closure {a, g⁻¹ * a * g} : Set H.normalizer).Finite := by
    refine Set.Finite.of_finite_image (f := H.normalizer.subtype) ?_
      H.normalizer.subtype_injective.injOn
    rw [← Subgroup.coe_map, MonoidHom.map_closure, Set.image_pair]
    exact Set.finite_coe_iff.mp (hG (a : G) ((g : G)⁻¹ * a * g))
  -- Its image in `N_G(H)/H` is `⟨ā, ā^ḡ⟩`, which is therefore finite as well.
  have h₂ : (Subgroup.closure {a, g⁻¹ * a * g}).map
      (QuotientGroup.mk' (H.subgroupOf H.normalizer)) = Subgroup.closure
        {QuotientGroup.mk a,
          (QuotientGroup.mk g)⁻¹ * QuotientGroup.mk a * QuotientGroup.mk g} := by
    rw [MonoidHom.map_closure, Set.image_pair]
    rfl
  rw [← h₂]
  exact Set.finite_coe_iff.mpr (by rw [Subgroup.coe_map]; exact h₁.image _)

/--
Does there exist a periodic residually finite $F^{*}$-group (see Archive, 7.42) all of
whose Sylow subgroups are finite and which is not binary finite?

Here $G$ is an $F^{*}$-group if for every finite subgroup $H$ of $G$ and every element $a$
of prime order in $N_G(H)/H$, the subgroups $\langle a, a^g \rangle$, $g \in N_G(H)/H$, are
finite; a Sylow $p$-subgroup is a maximal $p$-subgroup; and $G$ is binary finite if any two
of its elements generate a finite subgroup.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«9.78» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G),
      Monoid.IsTorsion G ∧ IsResiduallyFinite G ∧ IsFStarGroup G ∧
      (∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime → ∀ P : Sylow p G, Finite P) ∧ ¬ IsBinaryFinite G := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«9.78»

modeling_decisions: F*-group definition: the Archive text of 7.42 was not available in the sandbox (no internet). I used the definition given in the decomposition notes, which coincides with my own recollection of the Archive entry: G is an F*-group if for every finite subgroup H and every element a of prime order in N_G(H)/H, all subgroups ⟨a, a^g⟩ (g ∈ N_G(H)/H) are finite (i.e. N_G(H)/H is 'conjugately biprimitively finite' for every finite H). A reviewer with access to the Archive should verify this wording — this is the main residual risk.
a^g is formalized as g⁻¹ * a * g (standard right-conjugation convention); since g ranges over the whole quotient, the direction is immaterial.

'Sylow subgroup' is taken in the sense used for arbitrary (infinite) groups: a maximal p-subgroup, which is exactly Mathlib's `Sylow p G`. Quantified over all primes p (`p.Prime →`), so `Sylow p G` is never used with a non-prime p.
'Periodic' is formalized as `Monoid.IsTorsion G` (every element has finite order).
Residually finite is formalized via finite-index normal subgroups rather than homomorphisms to finite groups; the two are equivalent.
The group is quantified as `G : Type` (universe 0), following the other Kourovka files (1_74, 19_25).

Four `@[category test]` lemmas with full proofs were added as basic API tests for the bespoke definitions (finite groups satisfy all three; binary finite ⇒ F*-group). The generic definitions (residually finite, binary finite) are kept in the problem file because the task restricts output to a single file; a maintainer may prefer to move them to FormalConjecturesForMathlib.
Boundary check: the trivial group satisfies all positive conjuncts but is binary finite, so the existential is not trivially satisfied.

/-!
# Conjecture 9.78

by V. P. Shunkov

Does there exist a periodic residually finite $F^*$-group (see Archive, 7.42) all of
whose Sylow subgroups are finite and which is not binary finite?

Here, following Archive problem 7.42, a group $G$ is an $F^*$-group if for every
finite subgroup $H$ of $G$, every element $a$ of prime order in $N_G(H)/H$ and every
$g \in N_G(H)/H$, the subgroup $\langle a, a^g \rangle$ is finite. A group is binary
finite if every two of its elements generate a finite subgroup. A Sylow $p$-subgroup
of an arbitrary group is a maximal $p$-subgroup.

The requirement that the group be residually finite is what distinguishes this
problem from Archive problem 7.42.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«9.78»

variable (G : Type*) [Group G]

/-- A group $G$ is residually finite if for every $g \neq 1$ there is a normal
subgroup $N$ of finite index in $G$ with $g \notin N$. -/
def IsResiduallyFinite : Prop :=
  ∀ g : G, g ≠ 1 → ∃ N : Subgroup G, N.Normal ∧ N.FiniteIndex ∧ g ∉ N

/-- A group $G$ is binary finite if every two elements of $G$ generate a finite
subgroup. -/
def IsBinaryFinite : Prop :=
  ∀ x y : G, Finite (Subgroup.closure {x, y})

/-- A group $G$ is an $F^*$-group (Archive, 7.42) if for every finite subgroup $H$ of
$G$, every element $a$ of prime order in $N_G(H)/H$ and every $g \in N_G(H)/H$, the
subgroup $\langle a, a^g \rangle$ of $N_G(H)/H$ is finite. Equivalently, any two
conjugate elements of prime order in $N_G(H)/H$ generate a finite subgroup. -/
def IsFStarGroup : Prop :=
  ∀ H : Subgroup G, Finite H →
    ∀ a g : H.normalizer ⧸ H.subgroupOf H.normalizer,
      (orderOf a).Prime → Finite (Subgroup.closure {a, g⁻¹ * a * g})

variable {G}

/-- Every finite group is residually finite. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsResiduallyFinite.of_finite [Finite G] : IsResiduallyFinite G :=
  fun _ hg => ⟨⊥, inferInstance, inferInstance, by simpa using hg⟩

/-- Every finite group is binary finite. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsBinaryFinite.of_finite [Finite G] : IsBinaryFinite G :=
  fun _ _ => inferInstance

/-- Every finite group is an $F^*$-group. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsFStarGroup.of_finite [Finite G] : IsFStarGroup G :=
  fun _ _ _ _ _ => inferInstance

/-- The infinite cyclic group $\mathbb{Z}$ is not binary finite. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem not_isBinaryFinite_multiplicative_int : ¬ IsBinaryFinite (Multiplicative ℤ) := by
  intro h
  have hfin := h (Multiplicative.ofAdd 1) (Multiplicative.ofAdd 1)
  rw [Set.pair_eq_singleton, ← Subgroup.zpowers_eq_closure] at hfin
  have : (Subgroup.zpowers (Multiplicative.ofAdd (1 : ℤ)) : Set (Multiplicative ℤ)).Infinite :=
    infinite_zpowers.mpr <| by
      rw [isOfFinOrder_ofAdd_iff, isOfFinAddOrder_iff_nsmul_eq_zero]
      simp
  exact this (Set.toFinite _)

/--
Does there exist a periodic residually finite $F^*$-group (see Archive, 7.42) all of
whose Sylow subgroups are finite and which is not binary finite?

Here "periodic" means that every element has finite order, and "all Sylow subgroups
are finite" means that for every prime $p$ every maximal $p$-subgroup is finite.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«9.78» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G),
      Monoid.IsTorsion G ∧ IsResiduallyFinite G ∧ IsFStarGroup G ∧
      (∀ (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (P : Sylow p G), Finite P) ∧
      ¬ IsBinaryFinite G := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«9.78»

          (H.normalizer ⧸ H.subgroupOf H.normalizer)))

/--
Does there exist a periodic residually finite $F^*$-group, in Shunkov's sense,
all of whose Sylow subgroups are finite and which is not binary finite?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«9.78» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G),
      Monoid.IsTorsion G ∧
      IsResiduallyFinite G ∧
      IsFStarGroup G ∧
      (∀ (p : ℕ), p.Prime → ∀ P : Sylow p G, Finite P) ∧
      ¬ IsBinaryFinite G := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«9.78»
modeling_decisions: Used `Monoid.IsTorsion G` for periodicity: every element has finite order.
Defined residual finiteness via normal finite-index subgroups separating every nonidentity element; this avoids restricting finite quotient groups to a fixed universe.
Used Mathlib's `Sylow p G`, whose definition is a maximal `p`-subgroup even for infinite groups, and required `Finite P` for every prime `p` and every such subgroup.
Defined Shunkov's `F^*` condition on the quotient `H.normalizer ⧸ H.subgroupOf H.normalizer`; the two conjugate elements are represented as `a` and `g⁻¹ * a * g`.
Defined binary finiteness as finiteness of the subgroup generated by each pair of elements, and stated the source's 'not binary finite' as its negation.
Quantified the sought group in `Type`, following the repository's convention for yes/no group-existence questions.
